what_it_does: Optical computers can do AI math using beams of light instead of electricity, which is potentially far more energy-efficient than conventional chips. However, to control the optical hardware you still need conventional electronic circuits called digital-to-analog converters (DACs) — circuits that translate digital numbers into precise electrical voltages. This paper focuses on the fact that those DACs consume a surprisingly large share of the total power budget, undermining the efficiency advantage that optical computing was supposed to provide. P-DAC proposes design techniques to reduce DAC power consumption in the control loop of an optical AI accelerator, specifically for devices called Mach-Zehnder modulators — components that bend and steer light to encode numbers. The goal is to recover the energy-efficiency promise of photonic (light-based) AI chips by making their electronic control circuitry cheaper to run.
